extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy and education (e.g., those studying Plato's Republic, philosophy of knowledge, or models of civic education)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts of Plato's Republic (Books VI–VII) describing standards for knowledge, education, and qualifications of rulers/guardians — including analogies (sun, line, cave), divisions of knowledge, and required curricula (arithmetic, geometry, dialectic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea of the Good (sun analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘That which imparts truth to the known and the power of knowing to the knower’ — the idea of the good is the cause of science and truth, more beautiful and higher than either.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good is likened to the sun: as the sun makes visible things visible and is cause of growth though not itself generation, so the Good is author of knowledge and being though it is not mere essence. The Good is the ultimate object which must be apprehended with effort and which grounds reason and truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of reality: visible vs. intelligible (line analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reality is divided into two main spheres—visible and intelligible—each with further subdivisions (images/shadows and copies in the visible; hypothesis-based intelligibles and dialectical first principles in the intelligible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the divided line: first section (visible) contains shadows and reflections (images); the corresponding lower intelligible section uses those images hypothetically (e.g., geometry starting from assumed objects); the higher intelligible section proceeds through ideas to first principles via dialectic. Different degrees of truth correspond to these divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of cognitive faculties
rubrics_metrics.description: Four faculties of the soul correspond to the four divisions: reason (highest), understanding (second), faith/conviction (third), perception of shadows (lowest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each faculty has a clearness proportional to the truth of its object. This provides a scale for evaluating kinds of knowledge and the mental capacities appropriate to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between hypothesis-based enquiry and dialectic
rubrics_metrics.description: Some enquiries (geometry, arithmetic, allied sciences) proceed from accepted hypotheses and do not ascend to first principles; dialectic uses hypotheses only as steps to reach a principle above hypotheses and thus attains the highest knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometry and the 'arts' are valuable but intermediate: they employ hypotheses as starting points. True philosophical knowledge requires dialectical ascent beyond hypotheses to first principles (the Good).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegory of the Cave: stages of enlightenment and acclimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Humans are like chained prisoners seeing only shadows; liberation involves pain and disorientation as one turns toward light and ultimately perceives the sun (the Good).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ascent is gradual: shadows → reflections → objects → moon/stars → sun; sight (and the soul's eye) must be trained to endure greater light. Returning to the cave leaves one temporarily disadvantaged and possibly ridiculed; one must be prepared to endure difficulties in re-entering public life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as conversion, not implantation
rubrics_metrics.description: The power and capacity for learning already exists in the soul; education must turn the soul from the world of becoming to that of being rather than implanting sight where none existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers do not create knowledge from nothing; they facilitate the soul's reorientation. Effective education is an art that effects conversion, training the whole soul gradually to endure and apprehend the Good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and obligation of philosopher-rulers (guardians must descend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who attain the beatific vision of the Good must be compelled to descend and share in the labours and honours of the city rather than remain in the upper world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislators should not allow philosopher-rulers to remain apart; the happiness of the whole state outweighs individual preference. Rulers must be made benefactors of the state and participate in governance even if they prefer contemplative life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of true guardians/rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians should be the best minds, wise about affairs of state, rich in virtue and wisdom (not silver and gold), and possess the right education (both warrior and philosopher).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should be reluctant to rule (to avoid eagerness-driven rivalries), have broader honours/life than politics, and be trained to serve the common good rather than private advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular requirement: arithmetic as foundational
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic (number and calculation) is a study that compels the soul toward being, necessitates pure intelligence, and has both military and philosophical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arithmetic trains the mind to consider abstract unity and number in thought, resisting the intrusion of sensible particulars; it should be studied deeply (not as merchants) for its soul-forming power and practical military use (e.g., arranging troops).

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular requirement: geometry as contemplative science
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometry aims at knowledge of the eternal rather than the perishable and thus draws the soul toward truth and the spirit of philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometry should be sternly included in education; its true purpose is not merely practical applications (squaring, measuring) but to orient the mind toward immutable forms and being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge must be useful in war and public affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: The kind of knowledge that converts the soul must also, if possible, be useful in military affairs (guardian should be warrior-philosophers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects chosen for guardians must have dual utility: to elevate the soul philosophically and to serve practical needs of the state (e.g., arithmetic and geometry help military tactics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsuitability criteria for ruling
rubrics_metrics.description: Those uneducated in truth and those who never complete their education are unfit: the former lack a single aim to guide action; the latter will not act except under compulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete and properly directed education is a prerequisite for ministry of state; half-education or perpetual withdrawal into contemplation disqualifies one from effective governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological emphasis: abstraction and resistance to senses
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies that compel abstraction—forcing the mind to exclude visible/tangible objects and reason about thought-objects (e.g., indivisible unity in arithmetic)—help draw the soul toward true being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masters of such arts disdain introducing sensible particulars into argument; successful training emphasizes pure intelligence and consideration of entities 'realized in thought' rather than sensory instances.
